items.text: A pane's shell can be swapped in place: Restart Pane with Shell.
On Linux a Settings change keeps the config file's permissions and names its backup in local time, as on the Mac.
On Linux, Settings shows whether the session agent runs and lists your remote machines with Host Settings, as on the Mac.
On Linux, Settings > Appearance has the theme picker - one theme or a light and a dark one, a tile per theme, the filter - and the live preview, as on the Mac.
The command palette opens a tab, window or split on a shell you pick.
Right-click the tab strip's + to open a tab on any installed shell; File > New Tab lists the same shells.
A new pane takes a folder only from a pane of the same shell family: WSL to WSL, Windows to Windows.
On Linux, a viewer pane in a minimized or covered window stops polling git and animating, then catches up once when shown.
On Linux, a terminal pane left idle or out of sight gives back its drawing buffers and font copies, and draws afresh when needed.
